headline: Remember both product extremes
statement: Return the largest product of any nonempty contiguous subarray of nums. A single element is a valid subarray.
constraints: All subarray products and the answer fit a signed 32-bit integer
intuition: A negative number can turn the smallest negative product into the largest positive product. For that reason, save both the smallest and largest products ending at each position. For the next value, compare starting fresh with extending each of those two products.
approach: Initialize low, high, and best from the first value.
For each later value consider it alone and products with both old extremes.
Save the new extremes and update the global maximum.
correctness: Every ending subarray either starts at this value or extends a previous ending subarray. The old extreme products determine the new extremes under multiplication, whether the multiplier is positive, zero, or negative. Taking the maximum across endpoints covers all subarrays.
bruteForce: Multiply every subarray incrementally in O(n²) time.

complexity.explanation: Three product values summarize all previous positions.

pitfalls: Use old high and low together before overwriting either.
Zero may be the best possible subarray.
An all-negative singleton still requires a nonempty result.
